title: ARWP Data Authority Hypotheses
scope: Project experiments and source-backed quality constraints for data-rich websites. These hypotheses complement, but do not replace, registry/growth-hypotheses.json.

hypotheses.title: Distinct entity pages can capture useful long-tail demand
hypotheses.hypothesis: When a dataset record has real demand, unique attributes, a useful direct answer, stable identity and meaningful evidence, exposing it as a canonical human-readable page can create more useful Search and AI discovery opportunities than leaving the record only inside a bulk dataset or generic collection page.

checks.expect: The entity maps to a real information, comparison, navigation or decision need.
The page contributes non-commodity attributes, evidence, analysis, calculation or curation.
A direct landing visitor can use the page without navigating back to a parent database.
One stable canonical URL represents the entity.

hypotheses.title: Canonical HTML plus truthful machine-readable data may improve reuse
hypotheses.hypothesis: Publishing the same real record in useful canonical HTML and consistent Dataset/JSON/CSV/JSON-LD representations can improve dataset discovery and machine retrieval while reducing ambiguity, provided machine-readable data does not introduce facts absent from the public source of truth.

checks.expect: Important facts are visible to users in accessible HTML.
Machine-readable representations use the same identity and do not contradict visible facts.
Dataset metadata describes a real reusable corpus, not decorative structured data.

hypotheses.title: Meaningful entity relationships may improve deep discovery
hypotheses.hypothesis: Visible parent, related-entity, comparison and next-step links can make a large data site easier to browse and may improve discovery of valuable deep pages compared with an orphaned page factory or graph that exists only in JSON.

checks.expect: Relationships are useful to a person and visible in normal navigation/content.
Priority entity pages have crawlable internal paths from relevant collections or entities.
Edges represent real semantic relationships rather than keyword adjacency.

hypotheses.title: Quality gating should beat indiscriminate page expansion
hypotheses.hypothesis: For large generated sites, restricting indexable URLs to records with real demand and unique standalone value should produce a healthier experiment than publishing every possible entity/filter/query page and measuring success by page count.

checks.expect: Indexable candidates pass demand, unique-value, standalone-usefulness and canonical-identity gates.
Filter/search/query variants do not create uncontrolled duplicate indexable URLs.
Generated pages are not generic wrappers around minimal records.

successSignals: higher share of useful indexed pages
failureSignals: page growth without unique user value
